entities.name: Companion Planting
entities.description: The practice of growing different plants in proximity for mutual benefit, including pest control, pollination support, and improved yield.

hasChunks.text: Companion planting pairs plants that benefit each other — growing basil near tomatoes repels aphids and improves fruit flavour.
Three Sisters planting — corn, beans, and squash grown together — is the classic North American example of companion planting in practice.

entities.name: Crop Yield
entities.description: The measurable amount of agricultural produce harvested per unit area, typically expressed in kilograms per hectare or pounds per acre.

hasChunks.text: Improving crop yield depends on soil quality, water management, pollinator activity, and — increasingly — well-chosen companion plantings.

entities.name: Pest Damage
entities.description: The reduction in plant health or harvestable yield caused by insects, rodents, fungi, or other organisms feeding on or otherwise harming cultivated plants.

hasChunks.text: Pest damage can be significantly reduced through companion planting, encouraging natural predators, and rotating crops between seasons.
